title: Topological Charge-Transfer Excitons
authors: Huiyuan Zheng, Kaijie Yang, Ting Cao, Di Xiao
abstract: Excitons possess internal structure absent from single-particle Bloch particles, allowing their band topology to emerge from the bound-state structure rather than being inherited from their constituents. This raises the question of how the internal structure of a bound state can provide a microscopic origin of exciton topology. Here we show that the real-space embedding of charge-transfer excitons can generate an intrinsic manifold of symmetry-related off-site composite orbitals whose coupling supports topological exciton bands. Lateral electron-hole separation embeds the localized exciton on the bond connecting its constituent sites rather than on either site. We demonstrate this mechanism in a honeycomb lattice, where three bond-centered charge-transfer exciton orbitals form a Kagome lattice. By solving the Bethe-Salpeter equation, we show that this emergent multi-orbital manifold supports a topological exciton flat band upon time-reversal symmetry breaking, even when the electron and hole bands are topologically trivial. The resulting band exhibits nearly uniformly distributed quantum geometry, favorable for interaction-driven bosonic states. Our results establish a general route toward topological bands of localized composite bound states and unconventional strongly correlated bosonic phases.
summary: This work demonstrates that the internal structure of charge-transfer excitons can intrinsically generate topological band structures. By modeling these excitons on a Kagome lattice derived from off-site orbitals, the authors show that breaking time-reversal symmetry induces a robust topological flat band. This establishes a general theoretical pathway for engineering exotic correlated bosonic phases in condensed matter systems.
main_problem: To establish a microscopic origin for exciton topology arising from the internal structure of bound states, specifically using charge-transfer (CT) excitons where electron and hole are laterally separated.
main_result: The emergent multi-orbital manifold supports a topological exciton flat band upon time-reversal symmetry breaking, even when the constituent electron and hole bands are topologically trivial.
method: Solving the Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE) and analyzing the system's response to various symmetries ($	ext{T}$, $	ext{PI}$).
model_or_system: The study uses CT excitons in a honeycomb lattice, which form an intrinsic manifold of symmetry-related off-site composite orbitals that mimic a Kagome lattice structure.
key_observables: Exciton band structure, topological nature (Chern numbers) of the resulting flat band, and exciton quantum geometry (Berry curvature).
important_parameters: Hopping amplitudes ($t_c, t_v$), potential strength ($\Delta$), mass asymmetry ($m_e^*/m_h^*$), and symmetry breaking parameters ($\eta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the exciton structure arising from off-site orbitals rather than constituent bands; approximations include neglecting exchange interaction initially.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic electron-hole distributions, the resulting Kagome lattice of CT excitons, and the calculated band dispersions under various symmetry breaking conditions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical problem (CT exciton topology) to deriving an effective Hamiltonian on a Kagome manifold. It then uses continuum models and BSE calculations to analyze how $	ext{T}$ and $	ext{PI}$ symmetry breaking dictates the topological properties of the resulting flat band.
why_interesting: The concept of emergent topology in composite bound states, like excitons, provides an alternative route to realizing topological phases compared to engineering topology directly into single-particle bands, which is highly relevant for designing novel quantum materials and light-matter interactions.
